newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria c.bank denies T-bill sales to U.S. banks.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria c.bank denies T-bill sales to U.S. banks.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) rejected local media allegations on Tuesday that U.S. investment banks Merrill Lynch and J.P.Morgan have bought Bulgarian short-term treasury paper.

"Neither Merrill Lynch nor J.P. Morgan have purchased (Bulgarian) government securities through the BNB or other financial institutions," head of the BNB State Credits department Nikolina Micheva told Reuters.

The 24 Chasa daily said on Monday the two U.S. banks have demanded an additional weekly interest of 20 percent on one-month treasury bills they bought to compensate them for losses due to the lev's devaluation.
The lev fell to 208 to the dollar at the end of August from 187 a month earlier. It traded around 230 on Tuesday.
Other foreign banks have invested funds in lev-denominated T-bills, but the purchases were made through treasury paper dealers in the primary market, Micheva said.
"We had negotiations with Merrill Lynch for direct sale of treasury paper to them, but no deal has been finalised so far," said Micheva.
A Merrill Lynch analyst Andrew Kenningham confirmed the bank had not bought treasury paper on the Bulgarian market.
"We have not struck any deal with the BNB, but even if we had, an institution like ours cannot afford renegotiation of the terms of the deal," said Kenningham.

Foreign investment in lev-denominated Bulgarian government securities now totals around three billion levs ($13 million), down ten percent from the end of August, Micheva said. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
